rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from terminating tenancies without just cause and must provide relocation assistance for no-fault evictions, applicable to most residential properties not regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance after a tenant has lived in the unit for at least six months or their original lease expired, whichever comes first.

coverage.summary: Covers most residential properties in Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, after a 6-month residency or lease expiration.
coverage.owner_condition: Exemptions include owner's roommate and certain properties owned by HACLA or the government.
coverage.unresolvable: Tenant length of residency (at least six months) or lease expiration required.

rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, non-profit facilities for the homeless, short-term treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Minimum Rent Owed Threshold for Eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the unpaid amount is higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR) corresponding to the unit's bedroom size.

coverage.summary: Applies to all RSO and JCO rental units.

rules.citation: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO) / RSO
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) Rent Limits
rules.requirement: State law AB 1482 limits annual rent increases to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, in buildings older than 15 years.

coverage.summary: Applies to buildings that are older than 15 years old on a rolling basis, with specific exclusions for single-family homes under certain conditions, deed-restricted units, and others.
coverage.owner_condition: Single-family homes and condominiums are exempt from state law if owned by a trust, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, and proper notice is given.

rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years, units restricted by deed or affordability covenants, certain dormitories, certain two-unit properties where the second unit is owner-occupied, and certain single-family homes/condos under corporate ownership with proper notice.
rules.quoted_span: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower.
